name: Ada Flynn
life: “I still remember my son repeating a story I'd only half checked.” People around Juniper Street know Ada by a small Saturday habit. Ada knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I read the wrong name to my son for years. I want him beside me when the right one goes up.
appearance: Ada has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Look for a long plait tucked inside the collar. Off duty, the familiar outfit is a black overshirt with pearl buttons with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. In conversation Ada turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Ada has a quick wit and an equally quick sense of shame. A joke is often Ada's way of finding out whether a room is friendly enough for a serious question.
agenda: To show the corrected name to the son.
family: Damian Neal is Ada’s half-sibling. Ada calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Damian leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *Overdue by a lifetime*, Damian says, “I wrote my crush's name under the flap. They're coming to the reading with their spouse.”
connections: Ari Lane. The two grown children in the story deserve to know what name will go up this time.

reactions.situation: The shopkeeper asks for a public correction
reactions.response: Ada agrees a place and size for the correction with the person who was named.

reactions.situation: A street musician can't finish a familiar song
reactions.response: Ada starts a quiet conversation with the most impatient onlookers so the musician can recover their own time.
